result.summary: Bumps the minimum supported Clang compiler version from 17.0 to 19.0 across CMake checks, CI environments, and documentation. It replaces the CMake check for aggregate CTAD with a check for C++20 CTAD on alias templates, configures clang-format to use the latest standard, and removes an obsolete libc++ workaround in fuzz testing.
result.problem: Supporting Clang versions below 19 blocks the use of C++20 Class Template Argument Deduction (CTAD) for alias templates and necessitates maintaining legacy compiler workarounds in the codebase.
evidence: PR description: '(For this bump, only C++20 CTAD will become available.)'
PR description surveys distribution availability showing Clang >=19 is packaged in Debian Bookworm, Ubuntu Noble, CentOS Stream, FreeBSD, and OpenSUSE, or users can fall back to GCC.
result.changed_since_previous: Added commit dropping an obsolete libc++-15/16 std::optional comparison workaround in src/test/fuzz/vecdeque.cpp and cleaned up redundant version wording in depends/README.md.
result.card: Bumps the minimum supported Clang compiler version from 17.0 to 19.0 across CMake checks, CI environments, and documentation. This enables adoption of C++20 Class Template Argument Deduction (CTAD) on alias templates and removes an obsolete libc++-16 comparison workaround in fuzz testing. Developers compiling natively with Clang older than 19.0 will need to upgrade or switch to GCC.

risk.why: Incorrect feature checks or version bumps could prematurely break native builds on developer machines using older Clang installations.
